newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HAS $307 MLN H1 FOREIGN INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HAS $307 MLN H1 FOREIGN INVESTMENT.

text.p: Bulgaria attracted $307.3 million in foreign investment in the first half, $24.8 million higher than 1996's total, a Foreign Investment Agency official said on Thursday.
"Foreign investment for the first half of this year totalled $307.3 million against $282.5 million last year," Lyudmil Mikhailov, head of the agency's Information Department told Reuters.
Comparative figures for the first half of 1996 were not available.

Since the beginning of 1992, Bulgaria has attracted foreign investment of $1.098 billion, agency figures showed. About 28 percent of that came from the first half of 1997 alone and 10 percent of the total was from foreign company reinvestments.
Financial stabilisation in the second quarter of this year and the new reformist government's moves to speed up privatisation have boosted foreign investment, Mikhailov said.
"Increased proceeds from privatisation deals have been the main source of foreign investment this year, so far. Investment by Bulgaria-registered foreign firms also rose," Mikhailov said.
In April, Bulgaria sold 60 percent of its soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya to Belgium's chemical and drug group Solvay SA for $160 million, the largest single foreign investment in Bulgaria since 1992.

In May, the Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex bought 70 percent of Devnya Cement for $44.5 million and South Korea's Daewoo Corp. acquired 70 percent of Interpred World Trade Centre in Sofia for $20 million in June.
Germany has been the largest investor in Bulgaria with a total $232.8 million invested since 1992, followed by Belgium with $171.6 million and the Netherlands with $71.1 million.

Bulgaria's industry has attracted $525.3 million, or 47.8 percent, of the total foreign investment since 1992, followed by the trade sector with $204.3 million and the finance sector with $140 million, figures showed.

Government plans to privatise the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company and the national carrier Balkan Airlines were expected to boost foreign investment in transport and telecommunications, which have attracted $73.7 million and 10.9 million, respectively, since 1992. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
